boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Maine Maritime Academy rituals, ceremonies, and maritime practices rooted in its Castine regimental culture.

cards.title: Take the Ship Jump
cards.subtitle: First-year rite at the training ship
cards.notes: Look for official fall coverage of the first-year ship jump, a supervised rite marking entry into life as a Mariner.
cards.short_summary: New students make a literal waterfront entrance into the Academy.
cards.evidence_claim: Maine Maritime says first-year students officially jump from the ship each fall; the tradition began in 1960 and remains a rite of passage.
cards.access_notes: Participation is an Academy-organized first-year activity; do not attempt independently.

cards.title: Watch the Rings Meet Seawater
cards.subtitle: Junior-class ring ceremony
cards.notes: Follow the junior class’s Ring Dance coverage to see the class-ring ceremony and its seawater-washing moment.
cards.short_summary: Juniors receive their rings and ceremonially wash them in seawater.
cards.evidence_claim: Maine Maritime documents the Junior Ring Dance, begun in 1963, where juniors receive rings and each has a ring washed in seawater.
cards.access_notes: This is a junior-class ceremony held at the end of the academic year.

cards.title: Learn the MMA March
cards.subtitle: Academy march and fight song
cards.notes: Listen for the MMA March at Academy occasions and follow the official lyrics and gesture notes rather than improvising them.
cards.short_summary: An alumnus’s march gives the Regiment and teams a dedicated musical rallying point.
cards.evidence_claim: Maine Maritime says alumnus Albert B. Bennett Jr. ’54 gifted the MMA March, first officially played at the 2015 Homecoming March On.
cards.access_notes: Observe or join only when the Academy schedules the march at an event.

cards.title: Start as a MUG
cards.subtitle: New-student regimental entry process
cards.notes: Read the new-student materials before arrival to understand RPT, the structured training period that begins the MUG experience.
cards.short_summary: New regimental students begin as Midshipmen Under Guidance during RPT.
cards.evidence_claim: Maine Maritime identifies Regimental Preparatory Training as the indoctrination and training period in which new students are called Midshipmen Under Guidance (MUGs).
cards.source_title: Regimental New Student — Maine Maritime Academy
cards.access_notes: Applies to students in the Academy’s regimental program; follow Commandant staff instructions.

cards.title: Catch the MUG Olympics
cards.subtitle: Regimental new-student competition
cards.notes: Use the Academy’s event archive or current new-student schedule to follow this early regimental competition.
cards.short_summary: The MUG Olympics is a documented annual-program event for incoming regimental students.
cards.evidence_claim: Maine Maritime’s regimental new-student page lists MUG Olympics among its important dates, and its streaming archive records the 2025 MUG Olympics.
cards.source_title: Regimental New Student — Maine Maritime Academy
cards.access_notes: A scheduled Academy event; verify the current year’s timetable before attending.

cards.title: See the Regiment Induct Its New Class
cards.subtitle: Ritchie Field ceremony
cards.notes: Follow the published induction schedule for the March On, drill review, and oath that complete MUG training.
cards.short_summary: The ceremony turns MUGs into fourth-class midshipmen through a formal oath.
cards.evidence_claim: Maine Maritime says the Regimental Induction Ceremony culminates MUG training when students take the Oath of Midshipmen and become 4/C Midshipmen.
cards.source_title: Regimental Induction Ceremony — Maine Maritime Academy
cards.access_notes: The Academy states that the ceremony is open to family and friends; verify the current year’s event page.

cards.title: Mark the Oath of Midshipmen
cards.subtitle: Induction-ceremony centerpiece
cards.notes: Watch the official induction coverage for the oath, which formally changes the class’s standing in the Regiment.
cards.short_summary: The oath is the formal threshold between MUG training and fourth-class status.
cards.evidence_claim: Maine Maritime states that MUGs take the Oath of Midshipmen at the Regimental Induction Ceremony and then become 4/C Midshipmen.
cards.source_title: Regimental Induction Ceremony — Maine Maritime Academy
cards.access_notes: Part of the Academy’s organized induction ceremony; observe published event guidance.

cards.title: Follow the Regimental March On
cards.subtitle: Formation preceding induction
cards.notes: Check the induction itinerary for the MUG formation and March On before the drill review and formal ceremony.
cards.short_summary: A formal procession carries the incoming class into its induction program.
cards.evidence_claim: Maine Maritime’s induction schedule includes MUGs forming up for a March On, and its ceremony page says the class conducts a March-On during induction.
cards.source_title: Regimental Induction Ceremony — Maine Maritime Academy
cards.access_notes: Occurs within the scheduled Regimental Induction Ceremony program.

cards.entity_name: George C. Previll Memorial Inter-Academy Monomoy Challenge
cards.title: Row the Monomoys
cards.subtitle: Annual inter-academy rowing challenge
cards.notes: Read the Academy’s Monomoy coverage for the annual race and seamanship challenge contested by maritime-academy teams.
cards.short_summary: Maine Maritime’s crew rows historic open lifeboats against peer academies.
cards.evidence_claim: Maine Maritime describes the Previll Memorial Inter-Academy Monomoy Challenge as an annual round-robin rowing and seamanship competition involving MMA.
cards.access_notes: Team participation is organized through the Academy’s regimental program.

cards.title: Row Out in a Monomoy
cards.subtitle: First-week Castine Harbor training
cards.notes: See how each MUG company is introduced to open-boat rowing in Castine Harbor during its first week of training.
cards.short_summary: Every MUG company gets an early encounter with the Academy’s rowing culture.
cards.evidence_claim: A 2026 Maine Maritime alumni-magazine article states that each MUG company rows twice during its first week at MMA as part of Regimental Preparatory Training.
cards.access_notes: This is supervised waterfront training for regimental students; follow Academy safety direction.
